newsitem.title: USA: SEC alleges N.J. muni adviser in kickback scheme.
newsitem.headline: SEC alleges N.J. muni adviser in kickback scheme.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission Thursday charged Joseph Galluzzi, a former financial adviser to Essex County, N.J., and other municipal bond issuers with participating in a "kickback scheme" that netted him more than $250,000.

SEC said First Fidelity Securities, now a part of First Union Corp, and AG Edwards and Sons Inc, a unit of AG Edwards Inc, paid Galluzzi the money in exchange for work on municipal bond deals in New Jersey.
First Fidelity previously settled with the SEC in the matter, without admitting or denying the charges, by paying penalties and fees totalling nearly $2.3 million.
Officials at AG Edwards said they would have a statement about the case shortly. The SEC said AG Edwards paid Galluzzi at least $82,086 under a "sham finder's agreement contract."
Galluzzi, 64, the former Treasurer of Springfield, N.J., has an unpublished telephone number and could not immediately be reached for comment.

In a statement, the SEC said the bond deals involved were sold by Essex County, the Essex County Improvement Authority, and the Township of Irvington between 1987 and 1993. The SEC, which said its investigation is continuing, said it is seeking to enjoin Galluzzi from future violations and seeks disgorgement of the kickbacks he received.
